correctness.rationale: The mathematics is correct. Differentiating the published posterior score-MGF gives κ2=σ²r', κ3=σ⁴r'', and κ4=σ⁶r'''. Pearson's inequality in cumulant form is κ2κ4+2κ2³-κ3² at least zero, which expands exactly to the package's score-jet inequality. Equality with positive variance means a two-point posterior; positivity of the Gaussian likelihood makes prior and posterior supports identical. Solving two-point mean, variance, and third central moment gives the displayed atom gap, support points, and posterior mass, and Bayes odds recover the prior weight. The package verifier correctly checks representative equal/strict/violating cases.

originality.rationale: Originality fails under the required implication standard. The focal 2026 source explicitly gives the posterior moment-generating function as an integral of the conditional score, hence all posterior cumulants are obtained by differentiation. The 2025 open Pearson treatment states the classical sharp inequality kurtosis at least skewness squared plus one and identifies boundary distributions as exactly two-valued. Substituting the score-derived second through fourth cumulants into that classical inequality gives the audited differential inequality immediately. The two-point support conclusion follows directly because a Gaussian likelihood is everywhere positive, and the reconstruction formulas are standard two-point moment algebra plus Bayes odds. This is a useful observation but is mechanically implied by published ingredients.
residual_risks: The complete focal and 1993 articles were not independently available through the full-text routes used in this run; however the rejection does not depend on asserting their whole-document coverage because the accessible focal MGF identity and open Pearson boundary theorem already imply the central score inequality and equality case.

value.rationale: Gaussian score realizability is a meaningful topic, but this particular result is a routine transformation of a newly published score-MGF identity by the century-old Pearson moment inequality, followed by standard two-point reconstruction algebra. Under the required value bar, correctness and practical interpretability do not make this mechanically implied corollary an independently worthwhile finding.

limitations: The complete focal and 1993 articles were not independently available through the full-text routes used in this run; however the rejection does not depend on asserting their whole-document coverage because the accessible focal MGF identity and open Pearson boundary theorem already imply the central score inequality and equality case.
